 The Cincinnati Bengals , coming off a huge win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 9, have every reason to be buyers at the NFL trade deadline.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But after not making a move in 2025 and only acquiring Khalil Herbert back in 2024, the Bengals would have to buck their recent trends if they are to make a move on deadline day.
 According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , that's exactly what the Bengals just did. Cincinnati is reportedly trading for Philadelphia Eagles edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie, sending a 2027 sixth-round pick to land the veteran edge rusher.
 Bengals trade with Eagles for Arnold Ebiketie
 "Sources: The Eagles aren't done, trading edge Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for 2027 6th round pick," Rapoport reports.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement While this move for the Bengals isn't a blockbuster addition for a linebacker or a safety, it is a quality move to improve the team's depth chart at edge rusher.
 Boye Mafe, Cedric Johnson, Myles Murphy, and Shemar Stewart currently make up the edge rusher group in Cincinnati, with Cashius Howell on injured reserve and will miss some time.
 The extra depth can't hurt, especially with how underwhelming Stewart has been. Ebiketie is only really a depth addition and will slot into a rotational spot like he has been with the Eagles this season.
 MORE : Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement He's played in nine games this season, but hasn't started once for Philadelphia. He has no sacks this year, but has 25 tackles and two quarterback hits.
 In his five-year NFL career, the first four years of it spent with the Falcons, Ebiketie has 16.5 sacks with 43 quarterback hits and 17 tackles for loss.
 He's a cheap rental edge rusher who should help out the Bengals' depth chart at a premium position. While not a massive move for the Bengals, this is a quality addition that only costs them a 2027 sixth-round pick, which isn't much at all.
